title: Machine-readable command output is corrupted by merging stderr into stdout
reasoning: _run appends stderr to stdout even when a command succeeds. Consumers parse the combined value as JSON or as one filesystem path. A benign warning can make valid JSON ambiguous or turn a valid Git root into a nonexistent path, which can make repository process ownership checks miss an active process.
reproduction: Return successful command output with stdout '/repo\n' and stderr 'warning'; after merging, _process_repository_root resolves the combined string rather than /repo.
recommendation: Preserve stdout and stderr separately. Parse stdout only and add separately redacted stderr to diagnostics after a failure.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied, and no visible test exercises successful commands that also produce stderr.
suggestedRegressionTest: Simulate successful git and JSON commands with valid stdout plus warning text on stderr and assert parsing uses stdout unchanged.
minimumFixScope: Change _run to retain separate streams and update machine-readable consumers and tests.
